title: adaptive-seed-scheduler-and-hash-partitioned-replay-mapper
author: Priya Menon
description: Introduce an adaptive seed scheduler and a hash-partitioned replay mapper to improve deterministic multi-worker replay fidelity and reduce sampling noise across GPUs. Motivation: current replay runner distributes traces unevenly under heterogeneous GPU pools and suffers from high quantile jitter when short tail bursts dominate a single worker. This PR implements: 1) Seed scheduler: online estimator that assigns synthetic seed traffic probabilities per epoch to reach target p95/p99 variance budgets without manual tuning. 2) Hash-partitioned replay mapper: deterministic split of sessions across workers by a configurable stable hash on session_id+seed, ensuring worker-local k/v cache priming and reproducible hotpath placement. 3) Epochal sample condenser: lightweight aggregator that merges micro-segments within an epoch to reduce noise from sub-100ms bursts while preserving peak events for tail analysis. 4) Tracer integration: emit kernel-boundary timestamps (cuda kernel start/stop markers) alongside throughput samples so we can align host-side latency with kernel-level activity. 5) Reporting: new cycle-aligned quantile aggregator and gpu-fidelity-normalization step added to the report pipeline to surface per-GPU variance and enable cross-cluster comparisons. Implementation notes: CLI flags for --adaptive-seeds and --hash-partitioning added to benchmark-runner; config schema extended under bench.replay.{scheduler,partitioner} with sane defaults; small refactor of runner/core to expose deterministic sharding hooks. Tests: synthetic multi-gpu CI job (bench/replay-integration) added; unit tests for scheduler estimator and mapper. Checklist: - [x] Feature implementation - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration job - [x] Docs (bench README) - [x] Perf baseline run included

review_comments: Jordan Reyes: The deterministic partitioning looks good but we should surface the hash function choice in docs to avoid accidental changes. Suggest adding a versioned hash constant.
Ethan Liu: Can you add a short synthetic run demonstrating reduced p99 jitter across a 4-GPU pool? The integration job should include an assertion on p99 variance for regression prevention.
Priya Menon (author): Added a versioned hash salt and included a bench/replay/p99-variance.test in the CI job. Integrated a short synthetic run summary in the PR description.
Mina Patel: Tracer payload looks fine; ensure payload size is bounded to avoid high cardinality in traces. Consider sampling kernel markers at 1 in N for very high-throughput runs.
Priya Menon: Bounded the tracer marker batch to 128 per request and made sampling configurable via bench.tracing.sample_rate.
Jordan Reyes: Approving after CI pass and the additional synthetic assertion.
release_notes: Added adaptive seed scheduling and deterministic hash-partitioned replay mapper to improve multi-worker replay stability and reduce p99/p99.9 jitter. New reporting metrics: cycle-aligned quantiles and per-GPU fidelity normalization. Opt-in via --adaptive-seeds and --hash-partitioning; no breaking changes to existing configs.
notes_on_benchmarking: Baseline run attached: 4xA100 heterogeneous sim, 1M sessions replay, adaptive seeds enabled. Result: p99 variance down 42% vs control, median throughput stable, slight 3% CPU overhead for scheduler bookkeeping. Full logs uploaded to internal benchmarking bucket.
safety_and_risks: Low. Deterministic hash partitioning changes only replay distribution; production serving unaffected. Tracer markers are size-bounded and disabled by default. Scheduler is opt-in to avoid behavior drift in existing benchmark suites.
user_impact: Tooling change only. Users of bench/replay who opt-in will get more stable quantiles and reproducible multi-worker replays. No runtime behavior change for hosted inference.
notes: This PR paved the way for follow-ups: adaptive cross-model seeding (ENG-2301) and autoscaling-aware partitioners that respect hot spot locality.
